audit_findings.title: Land-bank purchase-price liabilities may escape both OE and the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $1,312.689m liability at May 31, 2026, equal to 12.6% of $10,404m base equity value or $5.45 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Land-bank settlement cash flows classified as financing may be absent from OE, while the associated purchase-price liability is not deducted in the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The liabilities related to consolidated inventory not owned primarily represent the difference between the option exercise prices for the optioned land and the Company’s cash deposits.
audit_findings.explanation: This is an unresolved possibility, not yet a demonstrated valuation error, because takedown economics may ultimately enter inventory, cost of sales, and OE. However, the filed liability is large enough to materially affect value if any portion escapes both routes. The six-month filing also reports $166.819m of payments against these liabilities, confirming that the claims require cash settlement.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $1,312.689m balance and 2026 settlement cash flows to inventory costs and projected OE. Rerun with any uncaptured claim deducted from the bridge or its recurring settlements included in OE, but not both.

audit_findings.title: The $3.3 billion stakes bridge may double-count earnings already in OE
audit_findings.magnitude: $3,294.5m stakes bridge, equal to 31.7% of $10,404m base equity value or $13.68 per share; FY2025 included $78.225m of equity-method earnings and $130.166m of technology gains
audit_findings.mechanism: Income from separately added investments may remain in the OE numerator while the underlying investment value is also added through the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: We record our investments in these entities in our consolidated balance sheets as Investments in Unconsolidated Entities and our pro-rata share of the entities’ earnings or losses in our consolidated statements of operations as equity in earnings (losses) from unconsolidated entities within each of the respective segments.
audit_findings.explanation: The overlap is not conclusively demonstrated because the detailed OE adjustments were not supplied. It is nevertheless materially unresolved: the bridge addition is nearly one-third of base equity value, and filed earnings contain identifiable investment-related income. Purging portfolio interest income alone does not establish that equity-method earnings, carried interests, and fair-value gains were removed.
audit_findings.action: Prepare an asset-by-asset bridge-to-income reconciliation for every component of stakes_net, including associated liabilities and noncontrolling claims, then rerun OE after removing all income attributable to separately added assets.

audit_findings.title: All bridge cash may not be excess cash
audit_findings.magnitude: $2,091.695m added cash, equal to 20.1% of $10,404m base equity value or $8.68 per share; this includes $559.8m of Homebuilding cash held briefly in escrow
audit_findings.mechanism: Cash required for mortgage funding, escrow settlement, and ordinary operating liquidity is added to the bridge while the earnings supported by that capital remain in OE.
audit_findings.evidence: Without the facilities, the Financial Services segment would have to use cash from operations and other funding sources to finance its lending activities.
audit_findings.explanation: Adding the entire cash balance as excess is not supported. The filing demonstrates that at least $559.8m was escrow-related at the measurement date, while Financial Services also relies on liquidity to finance originations. The exact excess amount remains unresolved, but treating all $2.092bn as distributable is reasonably capable of materially overstating equity value.
audit_findings.action: Classify cash by segment and purpose, exclude escrow and restricted or customer-related balances, determine minimum operating and warehouse-support liquidity, and rerun the bridge using only distributable excess cash.

audit_findings.title: The anchor may capitalize a transitional $1.5 billion deposit build as permanent weakness
audit_findings.magnitude: $1,549.664m FY2025 deposit increase, equal to 4.1 times the $377.5m anchor; comparable increases were $1,631.783m in FY2024 and $554.766m in the first half of FY2026
audit_findings.mechanism: The deposit outflow directly depresses cash-based OE and therefore the anchor capitalized through every forecast year and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: This was offset by (1) an increase in inventories due to our growth strategy, strategic land purchases and construction costs of $151 million; (2) an increase in deposits and pre-acquisition costs on real estate of $1.5 billion as we increased the percentage of controlled homesites primarily as a result of option contracts with Millrose; (3) an increase in other assets of $186 million; and (4) a decrease in accounts payable and other liabilities of $691 million.
audit_findings.explanation: Whether the FY2025 build was transitional is unresolved, but its size makes the issue material. Fully treating it as recurring may understate sustainable OE. Conversely, the similarly large FY2024 increase and continued 2026 build show that recurring land-bank funding cannot simply be ignored, so an unsupported add-back could overstate value.
audit_findings.action: Build a deposit roll-forward separating initial program funding, option-maintenance fees, replenishment, takedown applications, forfeitures, and growth investment. Rerun the valuation using a filed-evidence steady-state maintenance charge rather than automatically retaining or reversing the full FY2025 outflow.

audit_findings.title: The earnings numerator uses a pre-Quarterra perimeter while the bridge is post-sale
audit_findings.mechanism: FY2025 OE includes the formerly consolidated Quarterra perimeter, while the May 2026 bridge reflects a retained noncontrolling investment and post-sale assets and liabilities.
audit_findings.evidence: In December 2025, we sold a majority interest in Quarterra Group, Inc ("Quarterra"), a subsidiary of our Multifamily segment, to TPG Real Estate (“TPG”), thus retaining a minority interest.
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter mismatch is demonstrated, but its valuation magnitude is not. The filing says the sale itself did not materially affect consolidated financial statements, yet that does not quantify Quarterra's contribution to normalized OE. FY2025 Multifamily reported a $75.455m operating loss, equal to 20.0% of the anchor, but the supplied record does not isolate Quarterra within that result or identify its amount in stakes_net.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile Quarterra's FY2025 earnings and cash flows, sale consideration, deconsolidated assets and liabilities, and retained-stake carrying value. Recast the anchor to the post-sale perimeter and verify that neither former subsidiary OE nor sale proceeds are double-counted.

audit_findings.title: Nonrecurring investment items are not demonstrably normalized
audit_findings.magnitude: $130.166m technology gain and $156.076m Millrose exchange loss, equal to 34.5% and 41.3% of the $377.5m anchor, respectively
audit_findings.mechanism: The technology gain can inflate OE while its investments are separately added in the bridge; the exchange loss can depress OE even though the post-exchange stake balance and reduced share count are already reflected.
audit_findings.evidence: Excluding mark-to-market gains on technology investments of $130.2 million and one-time loss of $156.1 million on the Millrose Properties, Inc. exchange offer ("Millrose Exchange Offer"), net earnings attributable to Lennar for the year ended November 30, 2025 were $2.1 billion, or $8.06 per diluted share.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing identifies both items and the cash-flow statement separately adjusts them, but the supplied valuation does not demonstrate how those adjustments entered the $377.5m OE anchor. Their opposing net effect is only $25.910m, but each item is individually large relative to the anchor and must be treated consistently with the bridge and share denominator.
audit_findings.action: Trace both pretax items and their tax effects through the OE worksheet. Remove the technology mark-to-market gain for investments added separately, test an add-back of the noncash and nondeductible exchange loss, and rerun using the same post-exchange shares and stake balances.
